description: Using Tammy's Head fires 10 Brimstone lasers in all directions simultaneously. Each laser deals your full Brimstone damage. One of the most powerful combos in the game, capable of clearing entire rooms and melting bosses instantly.

The Technology laser coils around the Brimstone beam and multiplies damage by 1.5, stacking with other multipliers. In Repentance the double-Brimstone upgrade (a second Brimstone, or Sulfur) replaces that 1.5x with its own 1.2x, so it can lower your damage.
Tech X takes priority and fires a Brimstone ring instead of its laser ring. The ring is larger, has a much wider hitbox, and Brimstone's tears down does not apply. One of the strongest beam builds.

Mom's Knife takes priority, and Brimstone's tears down does not apply. Each throw also launches a barrage of extra knives that cross the whole screen and do not return, each dealing 2x Isaac's damage in Repentance. A longer charge adds more knives: about 2-4 uncharged, 8-10 fully charged. Does not work with Azazel's own Brimstone.

In Repentance the beam poisons and explodes on the first enemy or obstacle it hits every other tick, for 10 plus twice Isaac's damage; without Soy Milk or Almond Milk that is two blasts per shot. Ipecac adds only +2 flat damage and no tears down. The blasts can hurt Isaac up close.
Each Epic Fetus missile explosion shoots 10 Brimstone lasers in all directions. Combines the missile's massive base damage with full Brimstone beams. Absolutely devastating room clear.
Isaac's bombs release ten Brimstone beams in all directions when they explode. In Repentance the beams do not get Sad Bombs' flat +25 damage.
The Brimstone laser gains homing, curving toward enemies. Massively improves consistency in rooms with mobile enemies or awkward layouts where a straight beam would miss.
Fires a spread of two Brimstone beams with no extra charge time. In Repentance 20/20 also brings a 0.8x damage multiplier, so it is not quite double damage.
Fires 3 Brimstone beams in a spread. The Inner Eye's fire rate penalty makes the charge slower, but the gain in damage per second is still larger than 20/20's.
Fires 4 Brimstone beams in a wide spread. Huge area coverage and damage output, though the fire rate penalty makes the charge noticeably slower.
Brimstone becomes variable-charge. You can release early for a thin weak beam or fully charge for a massive beam at 250% damage and 160% width. Adds tactical flexibility.
Brimstone takes priority but fires 3-5 additional beams in random directions alongside the main beam. Huge room coverage without Lung's fire rate penalty.
The beam gradually increases in size and damage the farther it travels, gaining +20% damage per tile of distance. Makes long-range beams deal significantly more than close-range ones.
Beams bounce off walls once, creating a second beam at full damage. Effectively doubles your coverage in enclosed rooms. The bounced beam can hit enemies the original missed.
In Repentance the beam goes through the wall and comes back in from the opposite side once, so one blast can hit the same enemies twice.
Enemies and pickups are pulled toward the beam while it fires, so more enemies stay in its path.
Spawns split tears when the beam hits the first enemy or obstacle. Adds splash damage around the beam's impact point.
Spawns two perpendicular beams at the first point where Brimstone contacts an enemy or wall. Creates a T-shaped attack pattern for better coverage.
The beam destroys enemy projectiles during each damage tick. Provides a defensive benefit while attacking, especially useful against bullet-hell bosses.
Brimstone fires automatically at full charge and continues indefinitely while holding fire. You can steer the beam direction with the joystick. Tears stat increases beam damage and width.

Like Soy Milk: the beam fires by itself at full charge, lasts as long as fire is held and can be aimed in any direction. It also gains random worm trinket effects, shuffling quickly, and a higher tears stat raises its damage and width.

In Repentance Eye of the Occult gives a crosshair you move, and Brimstone fires by itself at full charge. The beam leaves in a straight cardinal direction and bends toward the crosshair rather than aiming straight at it.
Brimstone fires automatically toward the crosshair at full charge. Frees up your movement to dodge while the beam fires directionally.
Tech.5 fires its random laser bursts while you charge Brimstone. Gives you constant chip damage during the charge phase so you're never doing zero DPS.
The Technology 2 continuous laser fires while you charge Brimstone. Similar to Tech.5 but constant instead of random. Steady damage during charge.
The beam wraps around Isaac in a circle once, then shoots straight. Creates an orbital attack zone before the beam extends. Unique but situational.
Upgrades Azazel's short-range Mini Brimstone into the full-length Brimstone laser. Removes Azazel's biggest weakness (short range) while keeping flight and black hearts.
Mom's Knife deals a multiple of Isaac's damage (2x while held, up to 6x on a charged throw in Repentance), so Polyphemus's (damage + 4) x 2 carries straight into every knife hit.
Each missile explosion shoots a ring of 10 knives out from the point of impact, on top of the missile's own blast.
At full charge, fires 3-5 additional knives in random directions alongside the main knife. Massive burst of knives fills the room.
Isaac holds one knife but throws two in 20/20's usual spread, with no fire rate penalty. In Repentance 20/20's 0.8x damage multiplier applies, so each knife hits a little softer.
Isaac holds one knife but throws three at once in The Inner Eye's spread, covering much more of the room.
The knife deals triple damage regardless of range. Proptosis's distance penalty doesn't apply to the knife, making this a pure 3x damage multiplier.
Isaac controls a floating knife that deals 2x damage per tick. No charge needed — just steer it into enemies for continuous high damage.
Enemies are pulled toward the knife, both while held and while thrown. Keeps targets in the knife's path for maximum hit count.
In Repentance the knife sometimes throws off bone shards while it touches an enemy, each shard dealing half of Isaac's damage.
In Repentance Technology no longer fires a laser of its own: when the knife is thrown, a laser links its tip to Isaac, like The Forgotten's club throw or Technology Zero.
The knife fires with a Tech X ring around it. Both the knife and ring deal damage independently, combining melee and ring damage.
Missiles shoot 10 Technology laser beams in all directions on explosion, with a +25 damage bonus. Turns each missile into a laser nova.
Fires two Tech X rings instead of one, each at 20/20's 0.8x damage multiplier in Repentance.
Tech X rings shoot out smaller split tears on hit. Adds splash damage around each ring impact.
Tech X rings can block enemy shots as they cross the room, but in Repentance only some of the time; the wiki marks this as needing more testing.
In Repentance the rings bounce off walls once, so each ring crosses the room a second time.
Rings bend inward toward enemies, substantially increasing the damage area as the ring curves to hit targets.
Fires 3-5 extra rings in a 30-degree spread with the main ring, each extra ring dealing 50-100% of the main ring's damage. In Repentance fire rate is divided by 3.1, so it charges more slowly.

Dr. Fetus bombs explode on contact, poison and leave a poison cloud, and Isaac is immune to his own bomb shots (not placed bombs). In Repentance Ipecac adds only +2 flat damage and no tears down, so the old huge damage boost is gone.
Pyromaniac heals Isaac from Ipecac's self-damage explosions. Turns Ipecac's main drawback into self-healing, making you nearly unkillable while dealing +40 damage per shot.
Host Hat grants immunity to Ipecac's self-damage explosions. Removes Ipecac's main risk without the healing benefit of Pyromaniac.

Missiles turn green and poison what they hit, and in Repentance every explosion leaves a cloud of poison gas. Repentance cut Ipecac's bonus here to a flat +2 damage, so the huge damage boost of older versions is gone.

Monstro's Lung fires its 14-tear barrage as Ipecac shots, each with +40 damage and poison. In Repentance Ipecac's tears down applies, so the charge takes about three times as long. The explosions can hurt Isaac, so keep your distance.
When an Ipecac tear lands it splits into four smaller explosive tears, each dealing half of Isaac's damage. The split explosions can still hurt Isaac, so Host Hat or Pyromaniac is a good partner.

An Ipecac tear that hits a wall or obstacle, but not an enemy, splits into two smaller explosive tears, and those can split again into chain reactions. The blasts can hurt Isaac, so Host Hat or Pyromaniac is a good partner.
In Repentance the Ludovico tear does not explode and does not get Ipecac's +40; it gets only a small flat damage bonus (+2 on the Ipecac page, +4 on the Ludovico page).

In Repentance the laser poisons and explodes where it hits an enemy or obstacle, for 10 plus twice Isaac's damage. Ipecac adds only +2 flat damage, and its 1/3 fire rate still applies. The blasts can hurt Isaac up close.
WARNING: Ipecac shots boomerang back toward Isaac and explode on contact. Extremely likely to self-damage. One of the most dangerous combinations in the game.

Soy Milk's fire rate fills the screen with weak Ipecac explosions. Its 0.2x damage multiplier cuts Ipecac's +40 too, but you fire 5.5 times as often, so damage per second ends up close to Ipecac alone. The explosions can still hurt Isaac.

Libra evens out your stats, and in Repentance it counts Soy Milk's trade (much faster tears, far less damage) as only a small gain, so you end up with all stats slightly above base. The large all-stats boost was older versions' behaviour.
Fires tear barrages continuously without needing to charge. The rapid auto-fire combined with Lung's spread creates a constant stream of projectile bursts.

Technology 2's laser takes the place of half of Soy Milk's tears. The laser ticks a fixed 15 times a second, so Soy Milk's fire rate does not speed it up; in Repentance the two items' damage downs no longer compound on it.
The rapid stream of tears blocks nearly all incoming enemy projectiles. Creates an almost impenetrable defensive wall in front of Isaac.

Enemies are pulled toward the stream of tears, which helps accuracy and makes up for Soy Milk's low knockback. But the rapid tears can also drag enemies erratically around the room, and the Strange Attractor page advises against the pair.
Each tiny tear gains significant damage at range from Lump of Coal. Since Soy Milk fires so many tears, the long-range damage bonus adds up quickly.
Lead Pencil fires a 12-tear burst after every 15 tears, so with Soy Milk's fire rate the bursts come very often.

Rock Bottom keeps your damage from dropping, so Soy Milk's huge fire rate up arrives without the visible damage loss. Soy Milk's 0.2x damage multiplier still applies underneath, which makes later damage ups very hard to show. Take Rock Bottom first.

Missile explosions can fire ten Sad Bombs tears in all directions, each dealing a flat 25 plus Isaac's damage, without Epic Fetus's multiplier. In Repentance this is only a chance that rises with luck, reaching 100% at 30 luck.
Isaac becomes immune to his own airstrikes and heals from them instead. Removes all self-damage risk and turns missed shots into healing opportunities.
Grants immunity to your own missile explosions. Removes the self-damage risk from Epic Fetus entirely.
Increased tear delay but massively increases missile blast radius and damage. Each missile becomes a devastating area bomb.
Missiles explode in a large cross-shaped blast pattern, each explosion dealing 0.75x damage. Dramatically increases the area of effect.
2-4 additional crosshairs orbit the main crosshair. Missiles fire onto each crosshair simultaneously, creating a carpet-bombing effect.
In Repentance only the Epic Fetus crosshair fires, with no separate Technology laser, but every missile explosion shoots ten Technology lasers in all directions.
In Repentance 20/20 removes Polyphemus's fire rate penalty and fires two tears per shot. What the pair does to damage is unclear: the wiki gives both a +5 flat bonus and a damage drop for it.
If Rock Bottom is obtained first, Isaac keeps his original fire rate while receiving Polyphemus's massive damage boost. Eliminates the main downside entirely.
Dr. Fetus bombs grow and hit harder, becoming Mr. Mega bombs, and each leaves a regular bomb behind; in Repentance that second bomb deals a flat 100 damage. Polyphemus's fire rate down still applies.

No special interaction: both already give homing tears, so the pair adds Sacred Heart's 2.3x damage multiplier (and +1 damage) to Godhead's damaging aura. In Repentance the aura deals a flat 2 damage 30 times a second, so it does not grow with your damage.

The Ludovico tear grows and gains Godhead's damaging aura, and in Repentance it also homes, which can leave it stuck near enemies. The aura cannot hurt an enemy the tear itself is touching, so hold the aura over enemies rather than the tear.
In Repentance each tear's aura grows the farther the tear travels, but the aura's damage does not; Coal's distance bonus adds only to the tear itself.

In Repentance Soy Milk's 0.2x damage multiplier does not touch the aura, which deals a flat 2 damage 30 times a second, and Soy Milk puts far more homing, aura-carrying tears on screen. Soy Milk's smaller tears do shrink each aura.

In Repentance the barrage scales with charge: half a charge fires the full barrage at normal damage and a full charge doubles tear damage, but charging takes longer, so damage per second falls to about 80% of Monstro's Lung alone.

Monstro's Lung fires 12 Technology lasers in a 30-degree spread that arc 3 to 4 times and can hit an enemy more than once. Its tears down is not applied, but the charge takes just as long. Each multi-shot item adds 12 more lasers.
Monstro's Lung takes over: each charged shot fires 6 mini-bombs that go off at different times, without Dr. Fetus's tears down. Each multi-shot item adds one bomb, up to 21.
Your own bomb shots heal you instead of dealing self-damage. Turns Dr. Fetus into a safe healing weapon. Fire freely at close range.
Bomb projectiles home toward enemies. Removes the need to aim precisely, making Dr. Fetus much more consistent.
Bombs explode in a large cross-shaped pattern. Dramatically increases the area of effect of each shot.
In Repentance each fired bomb only has a chance to burst into Sad Bombs' 10 tears: 11% at 0 luck, plus 3% per point of luck, reaching 100% near 30 luck. Each tear deals 25 plus Isaac's damage.
Each bomb splits outward into 4 tiny bombs that go off almost at once, each dealing a flat 35 damage in Repentance.
Bombs split into 2 additional bombs on explosion that detonate almost instantly. Creates chain-explosion effects.
Fully charged shots deal massive Polyphemus-boosted damage. You can also tap-fire for rapid weak shots. Enormous damage ceiling with a flexible floor.
Charging makes Godhead's aura bigger but, in Repentance, not stronger: it still deals 2 damage 30 times a second. Chocolate Milk's charged tears themselves still hit for up to 4x damage.
Enemies, pickups and most bosses are pulled onto the floating tear, which keeps dealing damage while Isaac stays well away from them. A few immobile enemies are not moved.
Forms a large controllable Brimstone ring. No charge needed. Deals 15 damage ticks per second. Enemies inside the ring without touching it aren't hurt. Steer it onto enemies for massive DPS.
Kamikaze! gives an unlimited source of explosions, and Pyromaniac turns each one into healing instead of damage: half a red heart per use in Repentance.

Taking a hit spawns six troll bombs, and Pyromaniac turns their explosions into healing. In Repentance each explosion heals only half a red heart, so past Chapter 3 it no longer keeps up without The Wafer.

In statue form Isaac cannot be hurt while Daddy Longlegs stomps enemies, so most rooms and bosses can be cleared safely, if slowly. It cannot hurt bosses like The Shell and ignores enemies far from Isaac.
Become invulnerable while stationary. Cube of Meat orbits and deals contact damage to enemies that approach. Slow but completely safe room clears.
Become invulnerable while stationary. Ball of Bandages orbits and deals contact damage. Same principle as Cube of Meat — safe but slow.
Each tear that lands or hits something releases eight small tears instead of four: two sets of Cricket's Body's split.
Bone tears shatter into shards on hitting an enemy or obstacle, and each shard then splits into 4 smaller shards when it hits the ground.
The controllable Ludovico tear counts as consecutive hits while touching enemies. Quickly builds Dead Eye to max stacks for doubled damage.
Crown of Light doubles damage while all your red heart containers are full, and the 2x carries into the Brimstone beam. Taking damage switches the crown off for the rest of the room.
Crown of Light counts having no red heart containers as full health, so it is always on for The Lost: 2x damage. A hit that Holy Mantle absorbs does not switch it off.
Blank Card uses the held card twice, so a Two of Hearts, Diamonds and the like quadruple what Isaac has instead of doubling it. In Repentance Blank Card copies cards only, not runes.
Car Battery upgrades the pill effect Placebo copies. With 48 Hour Energy, for example, both batteries it drops are Lil' Batteries, enough for unlimited uses.

In Repentance 20/20 removes The Inner Eye's fire rate penalty, at the cost of a 0.8x damage multiplier. Each further copy of either item adds one more tear, with no further change to damage or fire rate.

In Repentance 20/20 removes Mutant Spider's fire rate penalty, at the cost of a 0.8x damage multiplier. Each further copy of either item adds one more tear, with no further change to damage or fire rate.
In Repentance Lead Pencil's 12-tear burst fires alongside the Brimstone beam every 4th blast, about every 2 seconds of beam time. Before Repentance, Brimstone overrode Lead Pencil.
Lead Pencil fires tear bursts periodically while the Ludovico tear is out. Gives you a secondary attack alongside the controllable tear.
Eve's Mascara gives 2x damage at 0.66x fire rate, and 20/20 adds a second tear at 0.8x damage without slowing fire. The multipliers stack, so each volley hits far harder than with either item alone.
In Repentance the beam deals 6x damage at point-blank range, then loses 13.3% per tile of distance, down to almost nothing at 7.5 tiles. Very strong up close.
Distance penalty is removed for Dr. Fetus bombs. All bombs get the damage multiplier regardless of range. Pure damage increase.
Spirit Sword overrides Brimstone: you swing the sword and fire its projectiles instead of a beam. Generally considered a downgrade.

With Ipecac, Revelation's holy laser poisons and sets off 8 explosions where it first hits an enemy or obstacle, each dealing 10 plus twice the laser's damage. The laser itself gets only +2 damage, not Ipecac's +40.
Four fetus tears fire alongside the Brimstone beam. With Soy Milk or Almond Milk, the fetuses fire continuously. Adds extra damage sources to Brimstone.
Fetus tears carry small spinning knives that deal extra contact damage on enemy hits. Adds knife damage to each fetus projectile.
Fetus tears explode on contact, poisoning enemies and dealing Ipecac's bonus damage. Each fetus becomes a homing explosive.
All new item pedestals cycle between two options. Massively increases your chances of finding strong items by giving you a choice on every pedestal.
Prevents unhelpful items (those with the nolostbr tag) from appearing and automatically re-rolls them. Ensures every item you see is useful for The Lost's build.
The Book of Belial becomes a passive held beneath another active item, and its damage boost scales with that item's charges. It may not work with single-use, unlimited-use or timed-recharge actives.
Whore of Babylon activates regardless of health. Dead Bird activates without taking damage. Both effects become permanent, giving Eve constant damage bonuses and a free familiar.
Brimstone beam becomes much wider with 2x larger collision area. Makes Azazel's already strong short-range beam cover a huge area.
Grants one red Heart Container and increases maximum heart limit to 18. Allows Magdalene to stack even more health for her tank playstyle.
Whenever a red Heart Container would have been gained, grants 2 Soul Hearts instead of 1. Doubles the value of every heart container pickup for ???.
Bloody Lust can grant 4 more damage boosts at +0.2 intervals, raising the maximum total to +14.0 damage. Makes Samson's rage mechanic scale even higher.
On death as Lazarus, Lazarus Risen gains +7.2 damage that fades at 0.12 per second. Killing enemies restores 0.07 damage. Rewards aggressive play after resurrection.
Spawns 3 random items from random item pools, and only one can be taken. It ignores item weight and can even offer items already taken this run.
Grants +1 Luck and nearly every floor spawns an upgraded Arcade with more machines, even without 5 coins. Great for resource generation.
Adds one Coin Heart and raises maximum Coin Heart limit to 4. More health capacity for a character who desperately needs it.

Any three Guppy items complete the Guppy transformation: flight, and in Repentance a 66% chance to spawn a Blue Fly each time a tear from Isaac or one of his familiars hits an enemy. With a high fire rate the flies pile up fast.

Any three Guppy items complete the Guppy transformation: flight, and in Repentance a 66% chance of a Blue Fly each time a tear hits. Dead Cat sets your red heart containers to one but gives nine extra lives, and the transformation makes up for the lost health.
Guppy's Paw converts red heart containers to Soul Hearts. Blue Baby has no red hearts, so the paw has no effect. It still counts toward the Guppy transformation if you pick it up.
Dead Cat gives 9 extra lives but sets health to 1. The Lost already has 0 health, so he just gets 9 extra lives with no downside. Also counts toward Guppy.
Dead Cat sets health to 1 heart container. For Keeper, this means 1 Coin Heart — a significant downgrade from his normal 2-3. The extra lives partially compensate but it's risky.
Brimstone's charge-up leaves The Lost vulnerable, but the massive damage per shot means fewer total shots needed per room. With Holy Mantle, the charge time is manageable.

Mom's Knife pierces enemies and passes through obstacles, hitting 20 times a second at 2x damage while held and 6x at about a third of a charge. Killing that fast suits a character who dies in one hit.
WARNING: Ipecac's self-damage from explosions is lethal for The Lost, who dies in one hit. Even with Holy Mantle, one close-range shot breaks your shield. Extremely risky.
Epic Fetus's missile self-damage can kill The Lost. However, the crosshair-guided targeting lets you aim far from yourself. Powerful but requires very careful positioning.
Polyphemus's huge damage per shot is ideal for The Lost — kill enemies quickly before they can hit you. The slower fire rate is acceptable given The Lost's one-hit nature.
Sacred Heart's 2.3x damage multiplier plus homing is perfect for The Lost. Homing tears reduce the need to position dangerously, and the damage melts rooms quickly.
Technology works as it does with Brimstone: its laser wraps around Azazel's short beam and adds the 1.5x damage multiplier, without making the beam longer.
Adds variable charging to Azazel's Mini Brimstone. Tap for quick weak beams or hold for powerful charged blasts. Increases Azazel's flexibility.
Curved Horn adds +2 flat damage to every tear. Most impactful with multi-hit or rapid-fire builds where the flat bonus applies many times per second.
Perfection gives +10 Luck and is destroyed if Isaac takes damage that isn't self-inflicted. That much luck maxes out effects such as Tough Love and Knockout Drops and takes Holy Light to its 50% cap.
Cancer gives +1.0 fire rate, a solid tears up for any build.
Every stat above Isaac's base (speed, range, shot speed, damage and, in Repentance, tears) gets 20% more of its excess: 4.5 damage becomes 4.7. The more stat ups a build has, the more it gains.

Doubles the fire rate of Isaac's familiars and halves the charge time of those with charged shots, such as Lil' Brimstone. Wisps are not affected, and Incubus and Twisted Pair gain less above about 10 fire rate.
All familiar tears gain homing. Transforms every shooting familiar into a homing turret. Extremely valuable with multiple familiars like Incubus or Twisted Pair.
Forgotten Lullaby doubles Incubus's fire rate, so it fires and charges faster than Isaac. The gain shrinks above about 10 fire rate, is gone by 27.5 and turns into a loss beyond that.
Baby-Bender gives familiars homing shots, so Incubus's copies of Isaac's tears home in as well. In Repentance they deal 75% of Isaac's damage unless he is playing Lilith.

Incubus follows Isaac and fires smaller copies of his tears, including some special attacks such as a Brimstone beam of its own. In Repentance it deals 75% of Isaac's damage unless he is playing Lilith.

Soy Milk undoes what makes Polyphemus special: its 0.2x damage cuts the huge (damage + 4) x 2 tears, and its 5.5x fire rate undoes Polyphemus's slow tears. You get many medium tears, about as strong overall as Polyphemus alone.
In Repentance Dr. Fetus overrides Brimstone: Isaac fires only bombs and the beam is lost. Firing bombs while charging the beam was Afterbirth and Afterbirth+ only.
Creates an energy orb that expands then shrinks while firing. You can charge a new beam immediately after. Unique mechanics but harder to aim, especially for Azazel.
WARNING: Tractor Beam forces the knife to snap to the firing direction, eliminating diagonal throwing. Reduces Mom's Knife's flexibility significantly.

In Repentance a thrown knife orbits Isaac very fast with a much larger hitbox, dealing steady damage on every side of him. In older versions this made the knife almost impossible to aim; that is no longer the case.
WARNING: Bob's Brain can easily self-damage The Lost with its explosion. Since The Lost dies in one hit, Bob's Brain is one of the most dangerous items to pick up.
WARNING: Kamikaze!'s explosion hurts Isaac. Holy Mantle absorbs the first blast, and the next one kills The Lost. Useless and actively dangerous.

In Repentance Tarot Cloth boosts only certain tarot cards; suit cards and runes no longer count. Strength doubles its stat ups (the damage multiplier once), The Empress quadruples its damage up, The Sun deals 400 damage to the room and The Stars gives a two-item Treasure Room.
Copies the effect of the card you are holding without using it up. It copies cards only, not runes, and its recharge depends on the card, from 1 room to 12.

Copies the effect of the pill you are holding without using it up, so a good pill can be taken again and again. In Repentance the recharge depends on the pill: stat-up pills take 6 rooms, and 48 Hour Energy, Balls of Steel and Full Health take 12.

With Almond Milk the Ludovico tear keeps teleporting around a small area, which makes it hard to aim. It hits more often, since the tear's hits per second follow your fire rate (up to 30), which offsets Almond Milk's 0.3x damage.

Epic Fetus keeps dropping missiles on Marked's crosshair on its own, while you move freely. In Repentance, if you dismiss the crosshair before the next missile drops, it still lands where the crosshair last was.
Adds a chance to fire Brimstone beams from all four cardinal directions simultaneously. When it triggers, you get a 4-way laser cross. Devastating in crowded rooms.
Adds a chance to fire a Brimstone beam from the back of Isaac's head simultaneously. When it triggers, you fire forward and backward at once.
A second knife permanently exists behind Isaac, dealing contact damage. You get a rear-facing knife that hits enemies approaching from behind.
Occasionally releases 1-3 extra knives in random directions when shooting. Free extra knives on top of your main throw.
As with Soy Milk, Libra counts Almond Milk as only a minor damage-per-second gain in Repentance, so the pair gives a very small all-stats up.
The laser makes a thin loop in front of Isaac and also fires a normal laser backwards.
In Repentance the knife's path does not change, but My Reflection's stat changes still apply: +1.5 damage, more range, 1.6x shot speed and -1 luck.
Enemies, pickups, and trinkets get drawn toward the crosshair. Clumps enemies together for the missile impact. Also conveniently gathers drops.
Soy Milk makes Technology fire 5.5 times as often, but every laser deals 0.2x damage, so damage per second ends up about where it was, spread over many weak lasers.
Each Technology laser hits with Polyphemus's damage, (damage + 4) x 2, and pierces everything in its line. You fire 0.42x as often in Repentance, since the laser's rate follows your tears stat.
In Repentance the laser deals 6x damage at point-blank range, falling to 0.1 damage by about 8 tiles away. Very strong up close and close to useless across a large room.
When a bomb explodes, its 10 tears become knives that fly out in every direction and do not come back. Turns every bomb into a knife burst.
Bombs explode into Technology beams in all directions. Combined with Tech X's ring damage, every bomb becomes a devastating multi-attack.
Car Battery makes The D6 reroll twice in a row, which gives no better pick and uses up the item pools twice as fast.
Car Battery makes Box of Friends add two copies of each familiar for the room instead of one, so you have three of each. With strong familiars like Incubus or Twisted Pair the damage adds up fast.
Each use gives two soul hearts instead of one. Using the book still brings a Harbinger in place of the floor's boss, as long as one can appear there and has not been met yet.
Each use gives two black hearts instead of one. Using it still makes the floor's boss drop a Devil Deal instead of its item, as it does in Repentance.
Each use spawns roughly twice as many blue flies: at least 4 instead of 2-4.
Car Battery makes each use of Mom's Box drop two trinkets instead of one, and holding the box still doubles the effects of many trinkets (72 of 188 in Repentance).
Sulfur activates twice, granting double Brimstone with a 1.2x damage multiplier for the current room. Extremely powerful temporary damage boost.
Car Battery's double-activation applies to every active item absorbed into Void. If Void has absorbed D6, Book of Revelations, etc., each triggers twice per use.
BFFS! doubles Incubus's damage. In Repentance Incubus deals 0.75x your damage unless you are Lilith, so with BFFS! its copies of your tears hit for 1.5x (2x as Lilith).
BFFS! doubles Twisted Pair's tear damage, so each of the two familiars hits for 0.75x your damage, with your fire rate, range, shot speed and tear effects.
BFFS! doubles the damage of Lil' Brimstone's thin beam: in Repentance 3 per tick becomes 6, for up to 48 damage per beam instead of 24.
Increases the Succubus aura radius. The damage multiplier inside the aura remains the same, but the larger area makes it easier to stay buffed during combat.
Hive Mind makes Infestation 2's blue spiders bigger and doubles their damage. Every enemy that dies, whatever kills it, leaves another spider, so they keep coming.
Hive Mind makes The Mulligan's blue flies bigger and doubles their damage. Each tear that hits has a 16.67% chance to spawn one, so a build that hits often makes more of them.

Restock refills the shop after each purchase and Steam Sale halves prices. In Repentance, outside Greed Mode, each restock adds to the price (+2, then +4, +6 and so on for items), and Steam Sale discounts only the base price, not that increase. Extra Steam Sales only divide the base price further (two make it a third), so the endless free shop of older versions is gone. Still a good way to turn coins into items.

With Chaos, Restock can restock the shop with otherwise rare items, and Steam Sale cuts their base price. In Repentance, outside Greed Mode, each restock adds to the price and the discount does not cover that increase, so the endless free shop of older versions no longer happens.

Once per room, Scapular gives you a soul heart when you drop to your last half heart. Getting hit charges Habit, so running into a hazard at low health charges your active item at little real cost. Leave and re-enter a room to reset Scapular.

4.5 Volt charges your active from the damage you deal, and Brimstone's piercing beam hits everything in its line many times per shot, so charges come fast. Still only one charge at a time, at 60 damage per charge on the first floor and more on each later stage.

Tech X's rings damage everything they pass through, 15 times a second, and 4.5 Volt turns that damage into active charges: 60 damage per charge on the first floor, more on later stages, one charge at a time.

The Ludovico tear deals constant damage while you hold it on an enemy, and 4.5 Volt turns that damage into active charges. Parked on a boss it keeps charging, one charge at a time, at 60 damage per charge on the first floor and more later.

Each use of The Book of Belial also spawns a black and red wisp in the middle ring that deals double a normal wisp's damage. Like other wisps it fires tears and blocks shots, on top of the book's +2 damage for the room.

Each use of The Satanic Bible also spawns a black wisp in the middle ring, shaped like an inverted cross, and each one raises the chance of a Devil Room by 10%. The black heart from the book still comes too.

In Repentance, absorbing The D6 into Void rerolls nothing that time. Later Void uses reroll the room's items before absorbing them, so the free pedestals are rerolled and then eaten, never kept as a reroll.

Void can use an absorbed Mega Mush every 6 charges instead of Mega Mush's 12 (every 4 in Repentance+). Each use makes you giant for 30 seconds: 4x damage, no damage taken, and you crush obstacles and break through doors.
Dull Razor triggers on-hit effects without actually losing health. Bloody Lust stacks damage per hit taken. Use Dull Razor repeatedly to max out Bloody Lust damage at zero health cost.
Dull Razor counts as taking damage for Cambion Conception without losing health. Repeatedly use it to spawn demon familiars (Incubus, Succubus, etc.) for free.

Using Diplopia on a Steam Sale gives you two. In Repentance n Steam Sales divide prices by n + 1, never below 1 cent, so two make a 15-cent item cost 5 instead of making shops free, and each further copy lowers prices less.

Holding fire for 2.35 seconds charges Maw of the Void, and letting go releases its black ring, which ticks 30 times at your damage, along with the charged Brimstone beam. It needs that full 2.35-second hold, not just a full Brimstone charge.

The Lost already has Holy Mantle's shield built in once it is unlocked. Picking up the item as The Lost in Repentance only adds one extra shield in the room where it was found; it is gone when you leave and does not come back.
Psy Fly orbits Isaac, chasing and blocking enemy shots, with a short cooldown after it blocks several. For The Lost that is a useful layer on top of Holy Mantle, though not immunity.

Dead Cat only cuts the form you pick it up as: as The Forgotten his bone hearts drop to 1 and The Soul keeps its soul hearts, and the other way round. After each death both come back with one bone heart and one soul heart.

Blood Oath drains Eve's red health at the start of each floor for damage and speed that last the floor, and leaves her low enough to switch on Whore of Babylon. The stab counts as damage, so Dead Bird's bird comes out too, for that first room.

Money = Power gives +0.04 damage per coin, up to +3.96 at 99. Keeper uses coins as health: a coin that heals him is spent, and in Repentance he pays for devil deals in coins, so his bonus drops whenever he heals or buys one.
Deep Pockets raises the coin cap to 999, and a room that would give no reward drops 1-3 coins instead. Keeper heals by picking up coins, so that means more healing.
Every 3 coins spent gives, in turn, +0.5 damage, +0.25 range and +0.03 speed. Keeper pays for devil deals and Black Market items in coins, so those count toward it too.
As Keeper, each use of IV Bag costs a Coin Heart and pays only 0-1 coins, and a coin that heals him is spent doing it, so the bag at best breaks even.
Lilith starts with Box of Friends and Incubus. Each use adds a copy of every familiar for the room, doubling her Incubus damage. More familiars, BFFS! and battery items make it stronger.

Lilith starts with Cambion Conception, so the hits she takes earn demon familiars: one each after 15 hits for the first two, then one after each further 30 hits for two more. A second Incubus is one of the possible results.

Blue Baby can't use red hearts, and Dark Bum collects them: every 1.5 red hearts gives a black heart 40% of the time, otherwise a card, rune, pill or spider. Hearts that were useless to him turn into health and pickups.
Abaddon converts all red hearts to black hearts. Since Blue Baby has no red hearts, there's no downside — he just gets the +1.5 damage, speed up, and fear tears for free.

Bethany starts with Book of Virtues and can use soul hearts as active item charges. She generates wisps from every active use, building a massive orbital army of firing, shot-blocking wisps over the run.
Incubus and most other familiars that follow Lilith stay stacked in front of her, facing the way she last shot, instead of trailing behind.
When Bethany spends soul charges to use her active item, half the time it costs her nothing.
Whichever brother picks up Birthright gains copies of the other brother's three most recently picked-up passive items.
As Lilith, Gello's tears deal her full damage instead of 0.75x. For the room it is used in, it fires alongside her Incubus with her damage, fire rate, range, shot speed and tear effects.

Lilith is blindfolded and fires nothing herself, but her Incubus copies her attack, so it fires the Brimstone beam at her full damage. Box of Friends, which she starts with, adds another Incubus and so another beam for the room.
WARNING: Abaddon replaces red heart containers with black hearts, which Keeper cannot use. In Repentance it no longer kills him outright, but it cuts his Coin Hearts down to one.

Only in Repentance+, where Infestation counts as a fly item, do these three complete Beelzebub: flight, small enemy flies turn into blue flies, and larger ones become friendly. In Repentance itself Infestation does not count.

These three books complete Bookworm: 25% of the time you fire an extra tear, at full damage in Repentance. Any three book items count, among them Book of Shadows, Book of Revelations, The Satanic Bible, Book of Secrets and Book of Virtues.

These three complete Seraphim: flight and 3 soul hearts. Other items that count include The Halo, Holy Mantle, The Bible, Rosary and Mitre; Guardian Angel and Sworn Protector no longer do in Repentance.

These three complete Leviathan, with Lord of the Pit counting from Repentance on: flight and 2 black hearts. Other items that count include The Mark, Spirit of the Night, Abaddon, Pentagram and Maw of the Void; Whore of Babylon does not.
Spun transformation: collecting 3 syringe items grants +2 damage and +0.15 speed. Any 3 syringe items work — includes Growth Hormones, Experimental Treatment, and various other syringes.
These three complete Conjoined: two tumor faces fire diagonally while you keep shooting forward, for -0.3 damage and -0.3 tears. In Repentance many other baby familiars count too.
These three complete Fun Guy, which gives one full red heart container. Any three mushroom items count, among them Odd Mushroom (Thick), 1UP, Blue Cap and Mega Mush.
These three complete Oh Crap, with Butt Bombs counting from Repentance on: each pile of poop destroyed heals half a red heart. In Repentance poop made by E. Coli heals too.
Holding all three bums turns them into one Super Bum, which picks up coins, red hearts and keys and drops twice the rewards the regular bums would. In Repentance its item drops come as two copies.
Swallowed Penny drops a coin when you take damage, and coins heal Keeper. In Repentance it drops 0 or 1 coins for Keeper, so it only sometimes refunds a hit.
Mom's Box doubles certain trinkets while held, Curved Horn among them: its +2 flat damage becomes +4, and +6 if the horn is also golden. A big flat damage boost for any build.
Mom's Box doubles the Cancer trinket's +1.0 fire rate to +2.0, and a golden Cancer with Mom's Box gives +3.0: a large flat tears up on any build.
In Repentance Cracked Crown adds 20% of the amount by which your speed, range, shot speed, damage and tears are above base, each stat on its own. Mom's Box doubles that bonus to 40%.

Perfection grants +10 Luck while held, destroyed on taking damage. The Lost with Holy Mantle rarely takes unshielded hits, keeping Perfection active for most of the run. Maximizes luck-based tear effects.
Perfection's +10 luck lifts Tough Love to its cap: from 9 luck every tear is a tooth that deals 3.2x Isaac's damage. Perfection breaks the first time you take damage that is not self-inflicted.

Perfection's +10 luck takes Holy Light to its cap, which is half your tears (50% from 8.89 luck). Each holy tear calls a beam of light dealing 3x the tear's damage to enemies in a small area. Perfection breaks the first time you take non-self damage.

Lilith attacks only through her Incubus, and Forgotten Lullaby doubles familiars' fire rate, so it works as a tears up for her whole offense and for any other familiars. The gain fades at high fire rates: none at about 27.5, and a loss beyond that.
Baby-Bender gives all familiar tears homing. Since Lilith fires through familiars only, this gives her entire offense homing — a massive accuracy boost with zero downside.

Forgotten Lullaby doubles familiars' fire rate, so both Twisted Pair demons shoot faster at normal fire rates. They follow Isaac's fire rate, so the gain fades above about 10, is gone at 27.5 and turns into a loss beyond that.

Baby-Bender gives familiars homing shots, so both Twisted Pair demons' tears track enemies. The demons float at Isaac's sides and fire with his tears, range, shot speed and tear effects at 0.375x damage each, and homing lets more of those shots land.

Mom's Purse lets you carry two different trinkets, so Curved Horn (+2 flat damage) and Cancer (+1.0 fire rate in Repentance) can be held together. In Repentance Mom's Purse also spawns a random trinket. Other strong pairings work too.
Cursed Eye fires a charged burst of five tears, but taking damage mid-charge teleports you to another room. The Lost dies to any real hit anyway, so the downside barely matters.
WARNING: Missing No. randomizes all passive items every floor. This can destroy a winning run by replacing powerful items with useless ones. One of the most dangerous items to pick up.

WARNING: Eve's Mascara doubles damage and cuts fire rate to 0.66x; Soy Milk multiplies fire rate by 5.5 and cuts damage to 0.2x. Together they mostly cancel out: fast tears that each hit for less than half your base damage.

Both multiply damage (Eve's Mascara 2x, Polyphemus (damage + 4) x 2) and both slow your tears (0.66x and 0.42x in Repentance). Together you fire about a quarter as often with huge tears: damage per second still rises, but crowds and fast enemies get harder.
In Repentance Dr. Fetus with Soy Milk rapidly fires low-damage mini-bombs, and the bombs no longer knock each other back as they did in older versions.

Both 20/20 tears count toward Dead Eye's multiplier when they hit (up to 2x after 4 hits), so it builds faster. A missed tear has a 20-50% chance to reset it, and 20/20 has a 0.8x damage multiplier in Repentance.

WARNING: The Wiz fires both tears diagonally outward, which makes them easier to miss. Each miss gives Dead Eye a chance to reset its multiplier (20% on the first miss, rising to 50%), so it rarely builds to its 2x.
Brimstone overrides Cursed Eye's charged burst, removing the teleportation risk entirely. You still get Brimstone's normal charge with no downside from Cursed Eye.
Mom's Knife overrides Cursed Eye's charged burst and removes the teleportation risk. You get the knife's normal behavior with no Cursed Eye downside.

Black Candle removes Cursed Eye's teleport when you are hit mid-charge, so you keep the charged burst of five tears (in Repentance) with no risk. It also gives curse immunity, a Black Heart and a better Devil or Angel Room chance.

Mom's Knife replaces Death's Touch's scythes, but its +1.5 damage still feeds the knife, which deals 2x Isaac's damage when held and up to 6x when thrown. The -0.3 tears comes along too, and the knife already pierces on its own.

Brimstone overrides the scythes and only Death's Touch's stats apply: +1.5 damage on every tick of the beam, but also -0.3 tears, which makes the beam charge a little slower since Brimstone's charge time follows fire rate.

Their x1.5 damage multipliers do not stack, so you get only one. The flat parts still add up: +0.5 damage from Cricket's Head, and +0.3 damage, +0.3 speed, +2.5 range and a heart container from Magic Mushroom.
Immaculate Heart's 1.2x damage multiplier applies to Brimstone. Additionally, orbital tears spawn and circle Isaac while the beam fires, adding extra hits to nearby enemies.
Sacred Heart's 2.3x and Immaculate Heart's 1.2x come from different groups, so they multiply to about 2.76x. Add Sacred Heart's homing and Immaculate Heart's orbiting spectral tears.

The star familiar slowly travels to the Boss Room and stays there for the floor. Standing in its aura gives 1.8x damage (1.2x in Repentance+), 2.5x fire rate, homing tears and a 50% chance to ignore damage; it gives no speed.
Damocles doubles all pedestal items but has a chance to instantly kill you after taking damage. Since The Lost dies in one hit anyway, the random death has no extra downside — pure double items.

While Damocles' sword hangs over you, item pedestals get a free extra item (not priced items or most chest items). Once you take damage that is not self-damage, the sword has a 1/10000 chance every 0.133 seconds to fall and kill you; that chance never grows. High risk, high reward.

In Repentance Stop Watch slows every enemy to 80% of its movement and attack speed, separate from and stacking with the slow status. Enemy shots are slowed too (and so are your tears), and it gives +0.3 speed.
Sacred Orb prevents items with quality 0-1 from appearing, automatically rerolling them. Ensures every item pedestal offers quality 2+ items. Dramatically improves run consistency.
Item pedestals rapidly cycle between 5 different items. Picking up the pedestal gives whichever item is showing. Skilled players can consistently grab the best option from 5 choices.

Restarts the entire run from Basement I while keeping all your items. Essentially doubles the length of your run, letting you collect items from every floor twice. One of the rarest and most powerful items.
Takes you to a special floor with one copy of almost every item you have unlocked. Take one and you return to the room you used it in. Pick the strongest item your run is missing.

Magic Mushroom's +0.3 damage and x1.5 multiplier stack with Polyphemus's (damage + 4) x 2, so each tear hits very hard. Magic Mushroom adds no fire rate, so Polyphemus's 0.42x fire rate stays as it is.

Cricket's Head's +0.5 damage and x1.5 multiplier stack with Polyphemus's (damage + 4) x 2, so each tear hits very hard, and a Polyphemus tear that kills carries its leftover damage on to the next enemy.
With Blood of the Martyr held, using The Book of Belial adds a x1.5 damage multiplier on top of its +2 damage for the room. That multiplier does not stack with Cricket's Head or Magic Mushroom.

Brimstone bombs gives +5 bombs, and each of your bombs fires four Brimstone lasers in the cardinal directions when it explodes, dealing 8 damage per tick for up to 19 hits. The lasers cannot hurt you.

With Dr. Fetus, each bomb shot only has a small chance to fire Brimstone Bombs' four lasers: 11% at 0 luck, reaching 100% at about 30 luck. The lasers can push your fired bombs around, so it is powerful but hazardous.
Each bomb you place fires Brimstone Bombs' four lasers in the cardinal directions (8 damage per tick) and Sad Bombs' ring of 10 tears (25 plus your damage each). Every bomb clears much of the room.

Psy Fly is an orbital fly that chases and blocks enemy shots; after blocking a number of them it rests briefly, still blocking but no longer chasing. It does not send shots back and is not full immunity. It also deals 15 contact damage per second.
BFFS! doubles familiars' contact damage, so Psy Fly deals 30 instead of 15 damage per second. Its blocking is unchanged: Psy Fly does not deflect shots, and BFFS!'s bigger size is only cosmetic.

The Book of Belial takes 3 charges, so 9 Volt gives one back each time you use it: its +2 damage for the room comes about every other room instead of every third. 9 Volt also fully charges the book when first picked up.

Guppy's Head takes one charge, so 9 Volt turns it into a 15-second timed recharge that runs while enemies are in the room. In a long fight you can call its 2-4 blue flies again and again instead of once per clear.

The Battery lets Blank Card store one extra charge, so you can copy the card you hold twice in a row. In Repentance Blank Card copies cards only, not runes, so Jera is out, and its recharge depends on the card copied.

Rune Bag drops a random rune every 7 or 8 rooms in Repentance, and D1 copies one random pickup in the room, runes included. The copy may be a different rune, and D1 must recharge, so there is no endless duplication.

Gnawed Leaf makes you an invulnerable statue after a second of standing still, while Daddy Longlegs keeps stomping (up to 40 damage about every 4 seconds) and Succubus's aura hurts enemies it bounces near (7.5-10 damage per second). A slow but safe clear, a bit faster with both.
Haemolacria takes priority: you fire arcing tears that burst into 4-7 Brimstone beams on impact, each dealing full damage per tick. Tear delay rises by 20 on top of Haemolacria's own tears down.

In Repentance Mom's Knife overrides Haemolacria, so there are no bursting knives. Its stats still apply: +1 damage and a x1.5 multiplier for the knife, but its fire rate penalty becomes +10 tear delay.

You fire arcing Ipecac shots that explode and then burst into poisonous, high-damage split tears; the split tears do not explode. Tear delay is a third longer than with either item alone, and in Repentance the two 0.8x range multipliers do not stack.
When a Haemolacria tear bursts, it also splits into Cricket's Body's four tears, and those can burst again. The burst tears themselves do not split. The two 0.8x range multipliers do not stack.
Haemolacria overrides The Ludovico Technique, so there is no controlled tear: you fire normal Haemolacria tears, which gain piercing.
Trisagion hides Godhead's aura, but the aura is still there and is not reduced by Trisagion's damage penalty. Godhead's homing carries over too.
With Spoon Bender's homing, Trisagion's blasts slow down and stay on top of an enemy, hitting it again and again (each blast can hit up to 15 times per second) instead of passing through.
Electric arcs jump between the Brimstone beam's contact points and nearby enemies. Adds chain lightning damage on top of the beam's already high DPS.
Tech X rings generate electric arcs that jump to nearby enemies as they pass. Adds chain lightning damage to the ring's contact damage for wider area coverage.
In Repentance Technology's lasers set off Jacob's Ladder sparks, which deal half the shot's damage and chain from enemy to enemy up to four times, so groups take extra hits.
Every tick of the Brimstone beam has a chance to summon a beam of holy light on the enemy. With a long beam hitting multiple enemies, this triggers frequently for massive bonus damage.
The beam sets enemies on fire without causing explosions. The burn damage stacks with beam damage ticks for additional DPS over time.
The laser turns yellow and each damage tick has a chance to drop a coin. Against rooms full of enemies, this generates significant income per beam.
Every other tick of the beam has a 25% chance to stick a spore on an enemy. Each spore bursts 2.5 seconds later for 5 damage, poisons nearby enemies and fires four homing spores in a cross.

The beam leaves a pool of creep at each enemy and obstacle it hits, every other tick. The pools are small and short-lived (30 damage per second, at most 25 each in Repentance), but several can hurt one enemy at once.
Rifts may appear where the beam hits rocks, walls, or enemies. The rifts pull in enemies and projectiles, adding crowd control alongside damage.
The beam has a chance to break rocks on every tick and gains extra knockback, and Terra adds +1 damage. It does not open Secret Room entrances or doors (Repentance+ lets lasers open doors).
Enemies killed by the beam are frozen solid. Frozen enemies can be kicked into other enemies for bonus damage.

In Repentance each tick of the beam has its own chance to deal Apple!'s 4x damage, rather than the whole beam getting it. The chance rises with luck (6.66% at 0, every tick at 14), and Apple! adds +0.3 tears.
Beam gains occasional 3.2x damage multiplier procs. At high luck this triggers very frequently, massively boosting beam DPS.
Each beam tick can mark enemies, causing them to be targeted by other enemies. Turns dense rooms into chaos as marked enemies get attacked by allies.
Shooting through Multidimensional Baby doubles the laser. Effectively creates a second beam for free if positioned correctly.
Any damage multiplier gained from Dead Eye before picking up Brimstone becomes permanent. A niche but powerful interaction if sequenced correctly.
The knife bounces as it flies away, with each bounce causing Isaac's tear damage. Adds extra hit opportunities at range.
Holy Light can trigger from both the held and the thrown knife. Each holy hit calls a beam of light that deals 3x your tear damage to enemies in a small area in Repentance.

A thrown knife leaves a line of creep behind it, laid at random intervals. The pools are small and short-lived (30 damage per second, at most 25 each in Repentance), but several can hurt one enemy at once.
The knife fires two knives in perpendicular directions from the first point of contact. Adds splash coverage to the knife's focused damage.
Isaac holds two knives that are shot diagonally. Doubles the knife output at the cost of cardinal direction aiming.
The knife flies toward Marked's crosshair and charges by itself. The farther the crosshair, the longer the charge and the throw; closer means shorter charges but faster throws.
The knife turns green and poisons, and a thrown knife explodes once per throw on contact on its way out, for 10 + 2.1x to 10 + 6x damage by charge. Ipecac's +40 damage becomes a flat +2.
Diplopia copies the Mom's Knife pedestal, and with two copies Isaac throws two knives at once, the second slightly angled. Each further copy adds a knife, up to 16.
Charging Spirit Sword's spin attack throws the sword a short distance, spinning as it flies, so the spin can hit enemies away from Isaac.
Dr. Fetus takes priority: each bomb flies inside a Tech X ring, and no charging is needed. The ring deals Isaac's damage and the bomb still explodes, so every shot hits two ways.
Tears burst into 3-5 Tech X rings of various sizes on impact, each dealing 100% of Isaac's damage. Massive spread of laser rings.
Enemies drop money based on damage tick frequency. The ring's multi-hit nature generates significant coin income per target.
Every 15th laser ring fires a cluster of tears alongside it. Adds periodic burst damage to the consistent ring output.
Loki's Horns' chance (25% plus 5% per luck) fires four rings at once, but only forward and backward, two stacked in each direction, not in all four directions.
Isaac sometimes fires an additional ring from the back of his head. Free bonus damage output without downside.
Ring deals 4.38x damage near Isaac but decreases with distance. Extremely powerful at close range for aggressive playstyles.
Damaging halo lost but homing retained. The ring bends inward to hit enemies within it, substantially increasing the damage area.
Tech X charges and fires full rings by itself, giving a steady stream of full-size rings. Soy Milk's 0.2x damage multiplier still applies, and a partial ring is hard to fire on purpose.
The ring poisons and explodes every other tick it touches an enemy, each blast dealing 10 plus twice the ring's damage, and the knockback pushes enemies along the ring. Ipecac's +40 drops to +2.
Tech X rings grow and gain damage the farther they get from Isaac. In Repentance they start at normal damage up close, but gain much less damage per tile.

Pick up Dead Eye before Tech X and its multiplier freezes where it was, up to 2x after four hits: misses no longer reset it, but it cannot grow. Taken after Tech X it does nothing, and saving and quitting clears it.
Fires a continuous linear laser while charging Tech X. Provides constant chip damage during the charge phase.
Occasionally fires a linear laser while charging Tech X. Adds random burst damage between ring shots.
Fetuses are surrounded by laser rings dealing half their damage. Adds ring damage to every fetus projectile.
Adds 25 flat damage to bomb explosions. A straightforward and significant damage boost to every bomb shot.
Each bomb explosion leaves a large pool of Mysterious Liquid's damaging creep, and overlapping pools can hurt an enemy at the same time.
Shot bombs can be detonated on command. Allows precise timing for maximum damage placement against moving targets.
Each bomb has a luck-based chance, 34% at 0 luck and certain from 8.25 luck, to split into 4-5 tiny bombs that deal half damage, spreading the blast wider.
Main tear scatters into 3-5 bombs that explode simultaneously. Massive area explosion coverage per shot.
The bombs home in on enemies, making them far easier to land, but they do not get Godhead's damaging aura.
You steer one bomb before it explodes, much as with Epic Fetus, and cannot fire another until it goes off. In Repentance the shot acts like Epic Fetus and gets Epic Fetus's synergies.
The bombs pierce and deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to each enemy they pass through. Eye of Belial's homing and doubled damage do not apply.
Every bomb leaves a fire behind after it explodes, as Hot Bombs do, which hurts enemies that touch it.
Little Horn's chance shots become black-tinted bombs that summon Big Horn's hand, killing a non-boss enemy outright or damaging a boss. Any bomb can be the instant kill.
Dr. Fetus fires Rocket in a Jar's fast rockets instead of bombs. They still explode on impact, and every synergy that would apply to the bombs carries over to the rockets.
Fired bombs stick to the enemies they touch, so they go off on target, and each explosion leaves slowing white creep. Kills from these bombs do not spawn Sticky Bombs' blue spiders.
Each strike becomes a barrage of two missiles in a row. 20/20's 0.8x damage multiplier weakens each missile, so it is less than double.
Each strike becomes a barrage of three missiles in a row, but The Inner Eye's 0.51x fire rate also slows how soon the next strike can be called.
Each strike becomes a barrage of four missiles in a row, but Mutant Spider's 0.42x fire rate also slows how soon the next strike can be called.
Incubus drops its own missile alongside each of Isaac's. Incubus deals 25% less damage for most characters, so the extra strike is weaker than Isaac's.
Each familiar calls a missile on its own crosshair, but those crosshairs are not synced with Isaac's and move much slower, so they stay near him and self-damage becomes much more likely.
Loki's Horns' chance (25% plus 5% per luck) spawns four crosshairs in the cardinal directions: Isaac steers one and the other three mirror it at a fixed spacing.
Missile explosions can spawn a pickup or trinket. In Repentance the chance falls by 1% with each spawn until the next floor, so a floor gives at most 63.
Every missile explosion leaves a large lasting pool of red creep. Creates massive persistent damage zones.
The crosshair slowly slides toward enemies, making missile targeting semi-automatic. Reduces precision needed for hits.
One smaller tear orbits the controlled tear and deals the same damage as it. 20/20's 0.8x damage multiplier applies to both.
The tear becomes a large spinning bone that sprays smaller spectral, piercing bone shots whenever it touches an enemy.
The tear becomes a large controllable laser ring dealing rapid damage at 1 tear delay rate. Full manual control of a Tech X-style ring.
The controlled tear releases holy beams periodically while touching an enemy. Constant bonus damage during sustained contact.
The controlled tear blocks enemy projectiles without disappearing. A mobile shield that also deals damage.
The tear becomes larger and deals more damage farther from Isaac. Encourages keeping distance while controlling the tear at range for max DPS.
The tear leaves a trail of creep pools at a steady interval as it moves. Mysterious Liquid's pools are small and short-lived, so the trail fades rather than staying.
A cluster of variably sized tears orbit the main tear, increasing the damage zone. No fire rate penalty since Ludovico takes priority.
My Reflection's 1.6x shot speed lets you move the controlled tear much faster and catch quick enemies. The tear also drifts slowly back toward Isaac.
The tear now and then flicks into a tooth that deals 3.2x damage before turning back. Higher luck makes it happen more often, and from 9 luck it stays a tooth.
The controlled tear bounces nonstop, a little slower than Isaac's fire rate, and each bounce splashes nearby enemies for 25% of Isaac's tear damage.
While holding a direction key, the Ludovico tear constantly shoots controllable tears in random directions. Adds offensive output while controlling the main tear.
Each time an Ipecac shot bounces it also explodes for half Isaac's damage on top of Flat Stone's splash, in a slightly wider radius. The bounce blasts can hurt Isaac.
Trisagion's blasts keep Ipecac's stats, poison, and explode on contact with enemies and obstacles, then keep exploding every tick against anything the first tick did not kill.
Maw of the Void's black ring hits far harder with Ipecac, poisons enemies, and explodes when it touches an enemy or obstacle.
Ipecac shots orbit Isaac for a long time. They land far enough away to spare him only if he stands still and they hit no enemy, so the blasts can still go off close to him.
Permanently grants the 6x fire rate multiplier from Kidney Stone after firing. Creates near-instant tear output permanently.
Red Stew's massive temporary +21.6 damage bonus becomes permanent. Locks in the full damage boost that normally decays over time.
All stat boosts from Purity remain active simultaneously. Grants permanent damage, fire rate, speed, and range boosts all at once.
Rock Bottom keeps Ipecac's +40 damage without its fire rate cut. With Brimstone or Tech X, take Ipecac first: in the other order Ipecac adds only +2 to the beam or ring.
Rock Bottom keeps each stat at its best D8 roll, so bad rolls cost nothing and repeated rerolls push damage, tears, range and speed toward 1.5-2x. A reroll only helps when it beats the best so far.
Eve's Mascara doubles damage while Rock Bottom holds fire rate and shot speed at their best. The 0.66x fire rate and -0.5 shot speed still count underneath, so later ups to those take longer to show.
Stat-down pills give False PHD's +0.6 damage (+1.2 for horse pills) while Rock Bottom keeps the lowered stat where it was. The drop still counts underneath, so that stat is harder to raise later.
Food items' speed downs no longer show, and every temporary boost, such as each food's +3.6 damage, stays at its peak. Each food taken from a cycling pedestal is a lasting gain, in place of the item.
Rock Bottom prevents the charge time increase, so Brimstone fires at near-normal fire rate. Dramatically increases beam DPS output.
If Dataminer's random stat changes push your tear rate to 120 before you take Rock Bottom, it stays at 120. The stat Dataminer lowered becomes harder to raise.
Rock Bottom stops 20/20's 0.8x damage multiplier from lowering damage, so the double shot comes without the drop. The multiplier still counts underneath, so later damage ups show less.
Sword becomes a lightsaber with a laser aura on every swing. Also deflects projectiles, combining offense and defense.
Sword and fired projectile become gigantic with massively increased damage. Charge time increases but damage is enormous.
Swing attack deals 9x Isaac's damage instead of 3x. One of the highest single-hit damage multipliers in the game.
Sword becomes larger. The projectile fires in an arc and splits on collision, creating a spread of burst tears alongside melee damage.
Both sword swings and fired projectiles can trigger Holy Light beams. Frequent melee hits mean frequent holy beam procs.
Sword swings reflect enemy projectiles back at them. Adds a powerful defensive ability to the melee weapon.
The sword's projectile bursts into several swords. A normal swing fires that projectile only at full red health, but the charged spin attack always launches one.

Each swing has Loki's Horns' chance to swing swords in all four directions, and a spin attack at that moment spins four ways. In Repentance the chance is 25% plus 5% per luck, reaching 100% at 15 luck.
Fired projectile becomes a Trisagion blast that pierces and deals continuous damage. Increases ranged attack utility significantly.
Isaac spins one additional time per extra tear, firing extra projectiles on each spin. Doubles projectile output of charged attacks.
Fetuses hold small swords and perform charged spin attacks as they travel. Each fetus becomes a miniature sword-wielding attacker.
With Mom's Knife the spin attack throws the sword a short way, spinning as it goes, and Technology adds a laser that joins the thrown sword to Isaac while it is in the air.
Launches a barrage of knives from Isaac's mouth after doing the spin attack. Combines melee with a ranged projectile burst.
Fires arcing tears that release Technology lasers in all directions upon impact. Each burst creates a starburst of piercing laser beams.
Fully charged shots and the tears they burst into are larger and deal more damage, and low-charge Haemolacria shots can be fired rapidly.
Main tears split on enemy/obstacle hits. Split tears can burst but don't split further, creating cascading projectiles.
Both main and burst tears increase the damage bonus. Missing burst tears doesn't reset the multiplier, making max damage easy to maintain.
Main tear bounces releasing burst tears on each bounce, with multiple bounces at high range. In Repentance, burst tears also bounce.
Lead Pencil fires 12 Haemolacria tears, all of which burst on impact. Creates an enormous volley of splitting projectiles.
Monstro's Lung takes priority: its charged shot fires 8 Haemolacria tears instead of 14, and every one of them bursts. Fire rate falls further than with Haemolacria alone.
Creates large tears that burst into standard tears unaffected by Proptosis damage falloff. The initial hit deals massive close-range damage.
Creates a large Trisagion beam that splits into more beams at maximum range. Combines piercing with burst mechanics.
Fully charged Trisagion blasts deal four times their normal damage, more than Isaac's usual tear damage, so the charge turns each piercing blast into a heavy hit.
Creates large stacking creep trails from each piercing hit. Deals significant passive damage as creep pools overlap heavily.
Lengthens blasts into flexible beams with larger damage areas. Increases the effective hitbox of each shot.
Every damage tick shoots a Pop! tear. Trisagion shots hover longer than normal, creating a field of bouncing tears.
Blasts deal 2x damage instead of the normal 0.33x, with minimal distance falloff. Massively boosts Trisagion's base damage.
Original blast shoots four white tears crosswise during travel and at range end. Adds splash to the piercing beam.
In Repentance the blast throws off Jacob's Ladder sparks on every tick it hits an enemy, not only when it meets an obstacle. Each spark can chain on to nearby enemies.
Spores stack multiple times on enemies due to the multi-hit nature. Creates rapid spore chain reactions.
Beam becomes a controllable Trisagion blast with high hit rate. Stays on enemies dealing continuous piercing damage.
Tiny tear bombs deal normal explosion damage despite Soy Milk's penalty. Massive fire rate creates constant sticky bombs on enemies.
Each tear hit keeps its 5% chance to drop a penny, and Soy Milk's fire rate lands far more hits than usual, so many more coins drop.
Every tear that hits an enemy has a 1 in 6 chance to spawn a blue fly, and Soy Milk's stream of tears lands so many hits that the flies arrive in a huge wave.
Every Soy Milk tear leaves its own creep pool, and the pools stack, so an enemy standing in the stream takes heavy damage even though each tear is weak.
Greatly increases knockback on rapid-fire tears, pinning enemies against walls. Turns the tear stream into a crowd control tool.
Fetuses become skeletons firing splitting bone fragments on enemy contact. Adds splash projectiles to every fetus hit.
Each fetus drops four short-ranged tears when it hits the ground, so every C Section shot ends in a small spread of tears.
C Section takes priority and Dr. Fetus' tears down does not apply. Each fetus drops one small bomb when it touches an enemy, its damage worked out with Dr. Fetus' formula from half the fetus' damage.
Fetuses zap nearby enemies with electric arcs on contact. Adds chain lightning damage to every fetus hit.
With C Section, Polyphemus's damage formula becomes a flat +5 damage and its fire rate down does not apply, so the fetuses hit harder at no cost.
Fetuses rapidly shoot short-ranged lasers facing enemies. Adds continuous laser output to each homing fetus.
Massive tears block enemy shots and continue, losing only 10 damage per blocked projectile. Acts as a shield that barely loses damage.
Both main and burst tears maintain all Godhead effects including the damaging aura. Splitting tears multiply the number of active auras.
Both main and split tears maintain the damaging aura and homing. Creates cascading homing aura-bearing projectiles.
Every split tear keeps all of Godhead's effects, so each split adds another homing tear with its own damaging aura.
The enlarged tear gains homing and a much larger, more powerful damaging aura. Massive single-shot damage potential.
All tears in the burst bounce simultaneously with greatly increased range. The bouncing barrage covers a much larger area.
Tears stay airborne longer and return to Isaac. Better reach and more focused blasts before the boomerang return.
The tears of the burst all follow the beam, at different heights, instead of spreading out, so many more of them hit the same target.
Instead of only the left eye's tears, each tear in Monstro's Lung's burst has a 50% chance to be a Blood Clot tear: larger, with +1 damage and more range.
The charged shot also throws out a large number of extra Immaculate Heart tears, which start orbiting Isaac once they reach orbit range.
In Repentance, when Loki's Horns triggers, the charged shot fires a full 14-tear barrage in each of the four directions. The chance is 25% plus 5% per luck, 100% at 15 luck.
Mom's Eye gives the charged shot a chance to fire backward as well, 50% plus 10% per luck in Repentance. In Repentance that backward shot is a whole barrage, not a single tear.
Fires automatically at full charge with random worm effects. Continuous barrages of tears with chaotic but effective coverage.
Technology's laser bounces off walls, and the rebound is a second beam that deals half damage.
In Repentance the laser wraps around the screen like Continuum's tears, keeping its momentum and coming back from behind Isaac, so one blast can hit an enemy twice.
The laser turns dark purple and fires on its own at a crosshair Isaac steers. The beam still leaves in a cardinal direction and bends toward the crosshair instead of aiming straight at it.
Tears that loop through the walls keep gaining A Lump of Coal's distance bonus, about +0.5 to 0.6 damage per tile with no cap, for as long as they keep wrapping.

Toxic Shock poisons every enemy as Isaac enters a room: 4 ticks on normal enemies and 2 on bosses in Repentance. Its page notes that high tear damage lets that poison kill enemies outright, and Polyphemus raises damage to (damage + 4) x 2.

While Isaac stands still as Gnawed Leaf's invulnerable statue, Sacrificial Dagger keeps orbiting, blocking shots and dealing 15 damage every 8 frames (112.5 per second in Repentance). Gnawed Leaf's page names it as stronger than most orbitals for this.
Each use of Box of Friends adds another Twisted Pair for the room: two more familiars with Isaac's tear effects, floating farther out and lined up beside the first pair to cover a wider area.
Twisted Pair's tears start from Isaac and follow Tractor Beam's beam, so both familiars' shots (0.375x damage each) join Isaac's own line of fire.
Creates a Godhead aura around the thrown head with homing. The aura damages enemies on the head's flight path.
Damaging aura expands once Explosivo attaches to an enemy. Growing aura damages nearby enemies while the explosive charges.
Damaging aura expands when Mucormycosis attaches. Growing auras and spore bursts create chain reactions.
In Repentance the laser releases a four-way spread of Cricket's Body tears whenever it hits a wall or an enemy, adding splash to the piercing beam.
In Repentance the laser splits into two perpendicular beams that deal full damage when it hits an obstacle or enemy. Repentance+ also adds small split tears.
Only in Repentance+: Car Battery makes Mega Blast's beam last half as long again, about 23 seconds instead of 15. In Repentance itself Car Battery has no effect on Mega Blast.
The Battery lets the active item hold one extra full charge, and Car Battery doubles or otherwise upgrades each use of an item it works on, so you can fire two upgraded uses back to back.

With 4.5 Volt the active item charges from the damage you deal instead of from cleared rooms. 9 Volt gives one charge back each time you use an item of two or more charges, so each use takes less damage to earn back. A one-charge item gets 9 Volt's 15-second timed recharge instead, and 4.5 Volt's damage still charges it too.
